appraisal_events.evidence: la manière mythologique et celle où il avait subi l'influence du Japon, toutes deux admirablement représentées, disait-on, dans la collection de Mme de Guermantes
appraisal_events.explanation: Reported opinion (an art review and hearsay 'disait-on') credits Mme de Guermantes' collection with admirable examples of Elstir's most acclaimed early periods, lending her prestige by association with his prized work.

status_effects.explanation: Being credited with owning admirable specimens of Elstir's most esteemed manners gives her modest prestige as a collector, though the claim is secondhand rather than narrator-endorsed.

ambiguities: The mention of Mme de Guermantes' collection is brief scene-setting for Elstir's oeuvre rather than a staged interaction; its status-conferring force is attributed to hearsay ('disait-on') and an art review rather than direct narratorial endorsement, so the prestige effect is kept modest.
Françoise and Saint-Loup appear only as incidental temporal markers (drawing curtains, waiting to go out) with no evaluative content, so they were omitted as peripheral.

Le narrateur functions throughout as the perceiving consciousness touring the studio; Elstir continuing to paint 'sur ma prière' is a minor courtesy but does not rise to a staged social outcome, so le narrateur was not scored.
